transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Ethan Brooks, Lina Chen, Jordan Ruiz, Priya Singh, Maya Patel

Summary: Quick procurement + legal alignment on MSA/DPA redlines, KMS options for Private deployment, and pricing approval path. Agree to exchange redlines and schedule pilot kickoff.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA data residency, KMS/HSM options, SLA expectations, pricing approvals, onboarding timeline.

[00:00] Ethan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Ethan from Redwood Inference here, Lina my SE is with me. quick roll call?
[00:14] Priya (Procurement): Priya here, hi.
[00:18] Jordan (Legal): Jordan Ruiz, legal counsel. Hello.
[00:21] Maya (CTO): Maya, CTO. Good afternoon.
[00:25] Lina (SE): Hi all. I'm Lina, I'll be owning the technical checklist and benchmarks.
[00:30] Ethan: Great. The goal today is to make sure procurement and legal are aligned on the outstanding MSA/DPA points and then confirm next steps for pilot/PO. We'll keep to 45 ish minutes.
[00:45] Jordan: Sounds good. We circulated a set of redlines last week; I want to go through the top 3 items — indemnity caps, data residency, and audit rights — and make sure we're aligned before I escalate pricing.
[01:05] Ethan: Perfect — Lina, do you want to cover the technical implications for the data residency options?
[01:12] Lina: Sure. For Lympha, you mentioned a Private/VPC deploy is preferred for PHI handling, right? We support Private with a customer VPC peering model, and we can integrate with KMS — we support AWS KMS and customer-managed HSMs for key management. There's a small network egress note: if you need on-prem, we need a slightly different packaging.
[01:36] Maya: Correct, Private is ideal. We are leaning toward customer-managed KMS; security team flagged that Redwood-managed keys are not acceptable.
[01:44] Ethan: Understood. Our Private offering allows customer-managed keys; we'll document the exact flow. We'll also include options if you prefer an on-prem appliance install — that has longer lead times.
[01:55] Jordan: On the DPA side, we want to lock in data residency and strict deletion timelines — 30 days after request for cache artifacts and 90 days for backups. Is that feasible?
[02:10] Lina: For the KV cache and model context, we can flush prefixes on deletion requests; operationally 30 days for residual logs is tight but doable with the right config. Backups 90 days is OK, though some infra providers may have retention at 90+; we can scope it.
[02:32] Priya: From procurement — cost is a blocker. Pricing we saw for Dedicated vs Hosted had a delta that needs internal approval. What's the recommended path to keep unit cost predictable?
[02:45] Ethan: There are three levers — Dedicated reserved capacity, Dedicated with burst, and Hosted with pinning. For predictable unit cost at scale, Dedicated reserved capacity is the usual. We can propose a committed monthly price and include burst credits. Pricing we share will show per-token and per-hour GPU cost, and Lina can send a modeled run-rate based on your estimated qps.
[03:10] Jordan: A couple contract items — audit rights: we need the right to audit annually, and indemnity: we'd like a mutual cap limited to fees paid in prior 12 months. Redwood's standard is a higher cap. Can you explain flexibility?
[03:28] Ethan: We can be flexible on indemnity — major customers often ask for a compromise. For audits, we support SOC2 reports and can enable audit logs with read-only exports; a full on-site audit requires a negotiated addendum, but we can offer attestations and a network of compliance docs initially.
[03:50] Jordan: Noted. We'll want to see the SOC2 report and the last penetration test summary.
[03:58] Ethan: We'll share SOC2 Type II and a redacted pen test summary — will include links in the redline packet. (shared: https://redwood.app/security/lympha-pack.pdf)
[04:10] Priya: About PO timing — if we can get redlines done by mid-March, our procurement can potentially issue a PO end of month. That affects whether we need a month-to-month or an annual commit.
[04:24] Ethan: Ok good — that aligns with our timeline. We'll aim to send redline MSA + DPA by 2026-03-17.
[04:30] Maya: Technical question — latency SLA. We need 95th percentile < 200ms for short prompts. Is that across your hosted or private run?
[04:41] Lina: On Dedicated with right GPU sizing and batching tuned, sub-200ms 95p is achievable for 512-token workloads. For Private, it depends on your network and peering; we can run a short benchmark.
[05:00] Maya: Great — would like a benchmark against our test set.
[05:05] Lina: I'll share the benchmark regimen and a sample script. We'll need sample prompts and a preferred region.
[05:12] Priya: One procurement nuance — we have an internal approval path that requires a third-party risk checklist and export control question. Jordan, will legal review that?
[05:22] Jordan: Yes we'll do it, but can you send a filled checklist? That helps speed approvals.
[05:28] Ethan: We'll fill the checklist and return. Also note that for export control items, we can flag model hosting regions.
[05:34] Jordan: On liability — the customer wants carve-outs for data processed that is regulated PHI. We need explicit language about Redwood not using customer data to improve models.
[05:44] Ethan: We have a clause restricting use of customer data for training for enterprise private deployments; we'll ensure the DPA has that language.
[05:51] Jordan: Please ensure it's explicit and not 'best efforts'.
[05:55] Ethan: Understood. We'll make it explicit.
[06:00] [06:00] Lina: Quick note: there may be small transcription errors in the earlier redline; we've flagged tokenization behaviour with certain health identifiers — will include mitigations.
[06:14] Maya: Also we require RBAC integration with our SSO (SAML). Is Redwood supporting SAML SCIM provisioning?
[06:23] Lina: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning supported; we also offer role mappings in the console and can set session timeouts per org.
[06:33] Priya: Procurement needs a clause about billing and invoicing net 60; Redwood default is net 30. Is net 60 something you can accept for enterprise?
[06:43] Ethan: For enterprise contracts, we can make concessions on payment terms with appropriate credit checks or escrow arrangements. We can propose net 45 or net 60 as part of the commercial terms.
[06:53] Jordan: Back to indemnity — mutual limitation to fees from prior 12 months — that's our preferred position. If Redwood needs a higher cap, maybe we can accept a carve-out for gross negligence.
[07:05] Ethan: That's typical language — we'll propose mutual cap tied to fees, with exceptions for willful misconduct and gross negligence.
[07:12] Maya: Regarding support and SLAs — what is the expected uptime SLA for Dedicated? And do you have credits or make-goods?
[07:23] Ethan: Dedicated carries an SLA with 99.9% uptime target and credits for missed targets; specifics depend on the reserved capacity commitment. We'll include the SLA matrix in the packet.
[07:33] Priya: For onboarding, can Redwood provide a deployment runbook and SSO/KMS contact points? Our security team will want a technical POC.
[07:42] Lina: Yes — we'll share a deployment runbook, network diagram, a sample terraform for peering, and the primary SSO/KMS integration checklist.
[07:50] Jordan: A small but important ask — can we get a short side letter that says Redwood will preserve audit logs for 3 years for legal hold scenarios? That's nonstandard but may be needed for certain payers.
[08:03] Ethan: 3 years is long; our standard is 1 year, with options to extend for an additional fee. We can discuss escalation paths — perhaps we can agree to a 2-year retention with add-on for 3 years. We'll propose options.
[08:18] Jordan: Ok please include the retention tiers and pricing for extension.
[08:23] Ethan: Noted.
[08:25] [08:25] Lina: Quick demo note — performance varies with batch sizes, we typically suggest continuous batching for throughput sensitive flows and small batch low-latency for synchronous calls. We'll include recommendation and config.
[08:40] Maya: How about support response times during the pilot? We need SLA for Sev1 response under 1 hour.
[08:48] Ethan: For pilot we can commit to 1 hour response for Sev1 via dedicated channel; post-pilot SLA will be formalized in the commercial SOW.
[08:58] Priya: On pricing approvals, are there discounts for multi-year commitments?
[09:04] Ethan: Yes, standard discounts for 12–36 month commits. Also volume tiers for token usage. We'll include modeled discount scenarios in the pricing spreadsheet.
[09:16] Jordan: Ok let's walk through the specific redlines we want changed — I'll read them, and Ethan or Lina can react. First: liability cap — swap Redwood's 10x fee to mutual fee cap.
[09:27] Ethan: We can propose mutual fee cap equal to the fees paid in prior 12 months. I'll flag that to legal and include optional escalations.
[09:35] Jordan: Next: deletion and retention — we want 30/90 as I mentioned.
[09:41] Lina: We'll add operational notes on how deletion will be executed and confirm backup retention timelines. There may be provider-specific caveats.
[09:50] Jordan: Next: training/use of data — add explicit prohibition on using data to improve models.
[09:57] Ethan: We'll add explicit language for private deployments; for hosted there's a separate consent flow.
[10:04] Priya: Payment and invoice — net 60 request noted.
[10:07] Ethan: We'll include payment term options.
[10:10] Maya: One more tech ask — can Redwood sign a BAA? We handle PHI.
[10:16] Jordan: Yes please confirm Redwood's willingness to sign a BAA.
[10:20] Ethan: Redwood can sign a BAA for customers handling PHI in Private deployments. We'll include a template BAA.
[10:27] Priya: Great.
[10:30] [10:30] Lina: I'll note the items I need from you: sample prompt set for benchmarking, preferred region, and network kickoff contact.
[10:41] Maya: We'll share a 100-prompt test set and a contact for the network engineer.
[10:46] Priya: Procurement needs the vendor questionnaire returned by Friday—I'll send a link after this call.
[10:52] Jordan: We'll need to see the redline before legal signs off; timeline dependant.
[10:55] Ethan: Timeline recap: Redwood to send redlined MSA/DPA + SOC2 & pen test, Lina to share benchmarks, customer to return vendor questionnaire. Target PO by end of March.
[11:12] Priya: One small point — SLA credits calculation, can you send the formula used? We'll add it to the procurement package.
[11:20] Ethan: Yes, we'll include the SLA credits math and examples.
[11:27] Jordan: Regarding export controls and regionality, can you confirm models hosted in EU region won't replicate data to US?
[11:36] Lina: We can pin model instances to a region and disable cross-region replication; still need to confirm third-party providers for backups.
[11:46] Maya: Ok good.
[11:48] [11:48] Ethan: Anything else?
[11:51] Jordan: I think that's it from legal. We'll review the redline and come back with comments.
[11:56] Priya: Procurement will await redline and vendor questionnaire.
[12:00] Ethan: Great. Next steps: I'll send the redline + security pack 2026-03-17, Lina shares benchmarks 2026-03-18, schedule pilot kickoff week of 2026-03-24. If this hits procurement timeline, PO by 2026-03-31.
[12:15] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[12:17] Ethan: Thanks. Ending call.

References/Artifacts shared: https://redwood.app/security/lympha-pack.pdf, https://redwood.app/decks/lympha-onboarding-runbook.pdf, benchmark script gist (private link).

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attribution (Ethan/Lina) and some words like 'KV' transcribed as 'K V' in earlier extract.

End of transcript.
